analysis: The code retrieves a property value, checks if it has text (non-null, non-empty, non-whitespace) using StringUtils.hasText(), and if so, attempts to parse it to an integer via Integer.parseInt(). The parseInt method may throw NumberFormatException (a runtime exception) if the string is not a valid integer (e.g., "abc", "12.34", empty string after trimming, or out-of-range value). This exception is currently unhandled. Since the method’s intended behavior is to return the provided default value when the property is not found, it is reasonable to also return the default value when the property value is present but cannot be parsed as a valid integer. Therefore, it is advisable to catch the NumberFormatException within this code snippet and return the default value, making the method more robust.
